source.title: Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization
source.anchor: Appendix A.2, Lemma A.13 and its use of Proposition A.10(f), printed pp. 295–296 / PDF pp. 307–308.

target: Prove the midpoint-series bound, differentiate finite Euler approximants, and control both compensated derivative tails. These inputs belong to the proof of Appendix Lemma A.13.

searched_existing: The shared Lean library and the pinned Mathlib definitions of the real Euler log-Gamma approximants, summable real p-series, uniform convergence of dominated sums, and finite-sum differentiation.
planned_consumers: The log Gamma derivative identity on positive arguments and the simplex estimate in Lemma A.13.
reuse_plan.decision_reason: Use the existing real Euler approximant. Add the two derivative approximants, two shifted tail functions and two summands so that the finite and infinite calculations use the same terms throughout.

semantic_roundtrip.formalizer: Six real functions and six proved statements transported from the audited private declarations.
semantic_roundtrip.blind_decoder: Independent neutral reads covered the finite bounds, series, Euler derivatives, uniform limits and four boundary instances.
semantic_roundtrip.source_reviewer: Compared the source argument with the exact finite telescope and real derivative domains. A separate import audit compared the complete types and values of the twelve named declarations, including both generated auxiliary proofs.
semantic_roundtrip.remaining_semantic_delta: The midpoint estimate uses algebraic telescoping. The book relates it to an integral on each unit cell. The cell identity, the infinite Euler derivative, boundary extension and simplex maximum have separate proof obligations.

graph_contribution.functor_reason: All terms live in the shared real analysis library. The midpoint finite bounds feed the summability result. The finite Euler derivatives and uniform tail estimates enter the later derivative-limit argument.
graph_contribution.visual_review: The Book route exposes three highlighted statements from the same shared module. Verified reader traversal remains pending.

progress_updates.teaching_route: updated: The Online Learning Book links the midpoint bound with the finite Euler derivatives and both uniform tails.

website_surfaces: Online Learning Book, Appendix A.13 proof steps, shared declaration catalog and Lean Graph.

truth_boundary: The bounded midpoint series, the two derivatives of the finite approximants and the uniform convergence on closed positive intervals are established. The derivative of the limiting Gamma function, extension to zero and vertex maximum require additional results.

focused_checks: The named module compiled and was imported in a separate probe. Twelve complete streams were identical and twelve were recovered exactly under reversible declaration and binder-name substitutions. Both generated auxiliary proofs matched their old sources byte for byte.

All four consumer theorems compiled and were imported under the Tests module. The 19 proof-argument differences across their four types and the full parent calls are recorded in docs/contracts/online-gamma-curvature-estimates-v1/proof-attempts.json.
verification.independent_review: Individual proofs, both finite Euler derivative signs and both M-test applications were checked in full. Concrete consumer validation is recorded separately.

contributor.name: Ji Cheng with Codex assistance
contributor.role: Formalizer with distinct neutral decoder, independent source/body reviewer and independent executor.

salvage.reason: The finite Euler proof and initial imported probe had retained failed runs. Their scoped repairs preserved the frozen statements.

parallelism.expected_information_gain: Check the reciprocal-square bound and both finite derivatives before identifying the derivative of the limit.

cross_route_blind_spot_audit.evidence: The boundary consumers exercise a singular denominator under total division, inclusive Euler indices zero and one, and both endpoints of a closed interval.
cross_route_blind_spot_audit.canonical_route: Compare positive midpoint summands, differentiate Euler approximants, and apply summable majorants on bounded positive intervals.
cross_route_blind_spot_audit.selection_reason: The algebraic bound and analytic identification are independently visible in the shared graph.

reader_backpressure.exposition_evidence: Three reading cards distinguish the midpoint estimate from the auxiliary Euler differentiation and uniform-tail proofs.
